subject: Production-readiness signal set & MAP: criteria, tests, rollback cadence
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Anita Gupta <anita.gupta@pepperhealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-01-08T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Production-readiness signal set & MAP: criteria, tests, rollback cadence

Hi Anita —

Thanks again for the call yesterday. As promised I pulled together a concise mutual action plan (MAP) focused on defining what "evaluation success" looks like for the Pepper Health pilot and the concrete acceptance tests we recommend to reduce risk at cutover. Attached: pepper-MAP-v1.xlsx (action tracker) and eval-testcases.md (candidate test cases).

High-level: we propose a three-tier gate sequence during the 4-week pilot:
- Tier 1 (Smoke, day 0–3): Functionality checks + security baseline
  - sample prompt coverage: 40 canonical prompts (clinical triage, scheduling, patient messaging) must return syntactically valid outputs for 95% of prompts
  - no PII exfiltration incidents in sample set
  - single-request latency P95 < 450 ms (edge region: us-west)
- Tier 2 (Load & quality, week 1–3): Performance and quality under realistic traffic
  - steady-state throughput target: 60 requests/min sustained over a 1 hr window with 95th percentile latency < 550 ms
  - automated quality regression: model must not drop below baseline on the curated evaluation set by more than 3% (human-eval composite)
  - embedding similarity sanity: top-1 recall on canonical retrieval tasks > 88%
- Tier 3 (Cutover readiness, final week): Resilience + operational SLOs
  - < 1% error rate across traffic profile during a 4-hour canary run
  - cold-start P95 for burst traffic < 900 ms
  - tracing hooks and token-level cost metrics visible in Console

Exit gates (hard blockers) — pilot fails and requires remediation if any of the following occur:
- Security/compliance finding: any PII leakage or inability to produce requested audit logs
- Critical regression: quality drop > 7% on primary evaluation shard
- Stability failure: > 5% error rate during a non-overloaded validation window

Acceptance tests we propose (see eval-testcases.md for full list):
1) Regression suite (automated): 2k prompt variants, expected scoring thresholds + fuzzing for hallucination detection
2) Load test (k6): 1-hour sustained with traffic mix (70% short chat, 30% long generation), KV cache enabled
3) Failover test: deliberate node drain to verify fast fallback to alternate region/model variant without exceeding SLO budget
4) Privacy audit: red-team prompts + review of audit log completeness and KMS usage

Rollback triggers (operational cadence):
- Immediate rollback: any confirmed PII exfiltration or data-safety incident
- Rapid rollback (within 1 hour): sustained error rate > 3% for 30+ minutes during steady-state testing
- Controlled rollback: quality regression between 3–7% — pause rollout, patch prompt set or model config, re-run regression suite

Proposed owners and timing (high level):
- Redwood: test automation, load harness, observability dashboard (owner: Marcus) — deliver week-of Jan 12
- Pepper Health: sample prompt set + primary evaluation labels (owner: Anita) — deliver by Jan 10
- Joint: canary run and go/no-go meeting — schedule for Jan 20

Questions for you to confirm:
1) Are the latency targets above achievable given your expected client patterns?
2) Do you want Redwood to run red-team (privacy) tests or do you prefer to supply an internal reviewer?
3) Any regulatory requirements beyond SOC/SLA we should include in exit gates?

If that looks good, I can turn the attachment into a one-page action tracker and lock owners/dates.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Anita Gupta <anita.gupta@pepperhealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-01-09T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Production-readiness signal set & MAP: criteria, tests, rollback cadence

Marcus —

Thanks for the clear proposal. A few quick items from our side:
- Latency: our expected traffic is patient-facing bursts (peak windows at 10:00–11:00 and 15:00–16:00 PST). P95 targets you proposed look reasonable but can we set a secondary higher-latency threshold (P99) for long-form generation so we know expected tail behavior?
- Red-team: yes please — we would like Redwood to run the privacy/red-team suite and share anonymized findings (we'll provide a safe sample set).
- Regulatory: nothing beyond SOC today, but please make sure audit logs include user-agent and request-id at the token level for our compliance folks.

We can commit to delivering the canonical prompt set by Jan 10 and a labeled subset for quality baseline by Jan 13. Jan 20 can work for the canary — would you be able to run the canary in the us-west region that day?

Thanks — attaching a short internal note (pepper-MAP-v1.xlsx) that lists a few stakeholders and times.

—Anita
Director, Product Operations
Pepper Health

Subject: Re: Production-readiness signal set & MAP: criteria, tests, rollback cadence

Anita —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. On the P99 tail: noted — we'll add P99 thresholds to Tier 2 and the cutover canary run. For the canary we will execute in us-west and maintain a separate trace group to measure cold-start tails.

Red-team: Redwood will run the privacy suite on an anonymized dataset and share a one-page summary with findings and remediation steps (no raw outputs).

Audit logs: we'll surface request-id and user-agent in the Console for the pilot retention window (30 days). If you need longer retention we can discuss retention add-on.

Next steps:
- Marcus/Redwood deliverables: test harness + initial dashboard by Jan 12
- Pepper deliverables: canonical prompts by Jan 10, labeled subset by Jan 13
- Schedule canary & go/no-go review on Jan 20 (2h block) — I'll send a calendar invite once you confirm time window.

I'll update the attached tracker and drop the automation checklist into eval-testcases.md tonight.

Best,
Marcus
